parts:
Hello, the error persists even after updating the INLA package.

However, if I select some variables in the formula

```

pc.u = 1
pc.alpha = 0.01
pc.u.phi <- 0.5
pc.alpha.phi <- 2/3
overdisp.mean = 0
overdisp.prec = 0.4

hyper.prec = list(theta = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(5, 0.01)))
control.family <- list(hyper = list(rho = list(param = c(overdisp.mean,
                                                         overdisp.prec), initial = overdisp.mean)))


#' The formula
formula <-
  y ~ 0 +
  b0 +
  aridity_index.log +
  brights.sq +
  elevation +
  evis.log +
  #lst.days.sq +
  #lst.nights.sq +
  night_light2012.log +
  pets.sq +
  pop_2010.log +
  prec.log +
  # travel_hfa.sqr +
  # travel_time.sq +
  # wets.sq +
  f(s, model = spde) 

stk.full <- inla.stack(stk.e1, stk.p1)

#' The inla() call
mod.init <- inla(
  formula,
  family = "betabinomial",
  Ntrials = numtrials,
  control.family = control.family,
  data = inla.stack.data(stk.full),
  control.predictor = list(
    compute = TRUE,
    link = 1,
    A = inla.stack.A(stk.full)
  ),
  control.compute = list(
    dic = TRUE,
    waic = TRUE,
    cpo = TRUE,
    config = TRUE
  ),
  num.threads = 4
)

```
The model runs, implying that there could be a problem with some of my variables, but I can't really figure out which is the problem. Can correlation cause the error?
